page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. This instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing a total of 8 vCPUs. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA instruction sets. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge demonstrates performance characteristics typical of older-generation hardware. CPU performance measured via stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests falls into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. However, the instance achieves average tier results in Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, large-block read and write bandwidths reach average levels. Cryptographic and database operations, including Redis SET benchmarks and Passmark database tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Small LLM inference tasks using a 135M model perform at an average level, but scaling to a 7B model drops performance to the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge offers dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which provides predictable execution times but lower resource density compared to newer architectures. Because it lacks local storage and exhibits weak-to-average processing speeds, it is appropriate for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high-performance computing. Suitable applications include basic web serving, lightweight background workers, software compilation tasks, and small-scale development or testing environments that can tolerate legacy hardware performance profiles.
